title: Skip tests by platform capability, not OS; probe once and skip with reason
context: Stock Windows hosts reported 109 false test failures—not product bugs but test-setup failures due to missing binaries (mktemp) and unavailable platform features (symlinks without Developer Mode, locale control). Blanket win32 skips prevented tests from running on capable Windows hosts. Touches invariant(s): con_7217ab24ab (Regression guard: "Flaky test failure under parallelism: native tree-sitter module resolution race on Windows" must not recur.).
decision: Replace OS-based skip conditions with capability probes (canSymlink, LC_ALL/LANG support). Tests now skip conditionally with a reason when a platform lacks a required feature, rather than skipping blanket by OS. Use Node.js APIs (mkdtempSync) instead of shell binaries (mktemp) to eliminate external-tool dependencies.
consequences: Honest test results: no false failures on capable hosts, no false passes on incapable hosts
Capable Windows machines now run symlink and locale tests, not blanket-skip them
Skip reasons are explicit (e.g., 'host ignores LC_ALL/LANG'), surfacing platform capability gaps
Skip counts vary by host capability, not by OS—dev/CI discrepancies visible
alternatives_rejected: Keep blanket OS-based skips: loses coverage on capable Windows hosts, hides gaps
Only run tests on CI (Linux/macOS): creates dev/CI divergence, frustrates dev machines
Fail on untestable preconditions: false positives, breaks test suite appearance on valid hosts
